our_argument_summary: Part 5 Test 1 argues the dome's V13 Finsler formula is calibration-not-prediction on Sydney-Perth: (1) Indian Pacific 4,352 km was known reference data when V13 was built; (2) it matches a circuitous railway route, not geometric distance (~3,291 km flight); (3) the same V13 system fails by 73% on geometrically analogous SYD-BUE in V12, with V13's claimed -8.4% resting on undefined n(r); (4) NEW after EXP-554: dome's own disc-radius (20,015 km) implies rim circumference 125,760 km and 70 S-coastal circumference of order 111,800 km against measured ~13,700 km - factor-of-8 to -9 discrepancy that refraction cannot dissolve because ships move through water not light. Verdict: Misleading.

dome_code_analysis.calculation_pipeline: Test 1 cites dome SYD-PER 4,352 km vs globe 3,287 km; dome SYD-BUE V12 d = sqrt(r1^2 + r2^2 - 2*r1*r2*cos(dtheta)) with r_SYD=7160, r_BUE=7298, dtheta=25.5 deg -> 3,194 km (-73%). NEW Problem 4: disc radius 20,015 km -> rim 2pi*20,015 = 125,758.8 km; AE-mapping r_70S = 20,015 * (90-(-70))/180 = 20,015 * 160/180 = 17,791 km -> coastal 2pi*17,791 = 111,798.3 km; globe 70 S parallel = 2pi*6,371*cos70 = 13,691.4 km; claimed measured ~13,700 km.

holes_found.description: PROJECTION-CHOICE PRE-EMPT MISSING. Problem 4 computes the coastal circumference using the linear azimuthal-equidistant mapping (r = 20,015 * (90-phi)/180), giving r_70S ~ 17,791 km. But the dome's actual V12/V13 system uses a non-linear mapping H(r) = 8,537*exp(-r/8,619) and elliptic-integral arc lengths - NOT the AE mapping. A sophisticated defender will object: 'You computed against a strawman projection that isn't ours; under H(r) the 70 S radius is much smaller and your 111,800 km figure is meaningless.' The §7.1 source pre-empts this exact objection with a load-bearing sentence: 'any monotonic latitude->radius mapping that places Antarctica on or near the rim of a 20,015 km disc still yields a rim circumference of ~125,760 km and a coastal circumference of the same order. The disc radius, not the projection, sets the scale.' This sentence was NOT ported into Part 5 Test 1. The reader of the kill-shot tab encounters the AE-mapping number with no defence against the projection-substitution attack, and would have to navigate to §7.1 to find the rebuttal. This re-introduces a kill-shot/§7.1 asymmetry of the same shape as c2 h2 - EXP-554 closed the headline asymmetry but a smaller one remains. (sections.json:part5.html Problem 4 paragraph; counterpart in sections.json:part7.html idx ~5478 onwards.)
holes_found.recommendation: Port the §7.1 sentence into Part 5 Test 1 Problem 4, ideally between the AE-mapping computation and the 'No coordinate formula' sentence: 'Nor does projection choice rescue this: the V12/V13 system uses an exponential H(r) mapping instead of linear AE, but any monotonic latitude->radius mapping that places Antarctica on or near the rim of a 20,015 km disc yields a rim circumference of ~125,760 km and a coastal circumference of the same order. The disc radius, not the projection, sets the scale.' (~50 words; preserves Problem 4's flow.)

holes_found.description: EMPIRICAL '~13,700 km' ANCHOR UNSOURCED AND MISREPRESENTED. Problem 4 asserts: 'Satellite-tracked circumnavigation records and altimetry of the Antarctic coast measure ~13,700 km, consistent with the globe value 2pi*6,371*cos(70) = 13,691 km.' Three issues for a defender: (a) NO specific citation - no race record, no altimetry dataset, no NSIDC reference. (b) The 13,700 km figure is the 70 S PARALLEL CIRCUMFERENCE on a globe, not an actual ship route - ships cannot circumnavigate at 70 S year-round due to sea ice. Actual recorded Antarctic circumnavigations (Jon Sanders solo triple-circumnavigation 1986-1988, Antarctic Cup commercial courses) traverse 55-60 S and log ~20,000+ km per lap. (c) Published Antarctic coastline length depends on resolution: CIA World Factbook 17,968 km (smoothed); Australian Antarctic Division ~30,000 km (with islands/inlets). A defender will say: 'Your "~13,700 km measured" is a hypothetical circumpolar parallel, not a measurement. Cite a single actual circumnavigation log returning that value.' The argument's broad ratio still wins (~111,800/17,968 ~ 6.2x on the most sympathetic figure), but the factor-of-eight headline rests on a number that conflates a globe geometric calculation with a 'measurement' - a hostile reviewer would quote this against us as sleight-of-hand. ALSO PRESENT IN §7.1 (sections.json:part7.html idx ~5100) - same unsourced figure; parallel patch warranted.
holes_found.recommendation: Two paths. Path A (preferred): cite a specific source - e.g. CIA / IBCSO Antarctic coastline 17,968 km, and use that; ratio becomes 111,800/17,968 ~ 6.2x, factor-of-eight headline becomes factor-of-six. Lose 2x headline punch, gain bulletproof sourcing. Path B (lighter): keep ~13,700 km but explicitly disclose it is the 70 S parallel circumference and not a single recorded voyage: 'The 70 S parallel circumference is 2pi*6,371*cos(70) = 13,691 km; recorded southern-ocean circumnavigations at 55-60 S log ~20,000 km. Either number leaves a factor-of-6-to-9 discrepancy with the dome.' Either fixes the empirical-anchor weakness. §7.1 has the same issue and needs the same fix.

holes_found.description: MISSING V22 EVOLUTION-LOG CONCESSION. §7.1 cites the dome author's own admission: 'Version 22 concluded, in the specific context of cross-equatorial city-pair distances computed under V9/V11's circular-disc + WGS84 coordinate formula: "Southern arc distances 2x too long - FAILS. Globe wins cross-equator."' This is a powerful authority-from-the-defender quote: the dome's OWN author conceded southern-arc failure. Part 5 Test 1 does not include this concession, which deprives the kill-shot of one of its strongest debating moves (the dome admitting it failed). Defender risk: a reader of the kill-shot tab does not learn the author self-acknowledged a related failure mode. (sections.json:part7.html idx ~5600.)
holes_found.recommendation: Add one sentence to Problem 4 (after the rim/coast computation): 'The dome author has already conceded a related geometric failure: V22 (predecessor to V12) explicitly stated "Southern arc distances 2x too long - FAILS. Globe wins cross-equator." The rim circumference problem is the same family of failure at greater magnitude - factor of 8-9 rather than 2x - and it survives any coordinate-formula patch because it depends on the disc radius itself.' Ports §7.1's strongest authority quote without ballooning Problem 4.

holes_found.description: MISSING 'SEPARATE AND LARGER FAILURE' FRAMING. §7.1's closing structures the rim argument as orthogonal to the coordinate-formula debate: 'The rim circumnavigation problem is a separate and larger failure: a factor of 8-9, not 2x, and it follows from the disc radius itself rather than from any coordinate formula. It predates and supersedes all coordinate-formula debates.' Part 5 Test 1's Problem 4 does not draw this distinction. A reader may conflate the rim factor-of-8 with the SYD-BUE 73% as 'same kind of problem the V13 formula is trying to fix.' But they are different: 73% is a coordinate-formula error V12->V13 narrowed; factor-of-8 is set by the disc-radius parameter and cannot be narrowed by any coordinate formula short of replacing the disc radius itself. Without this framing, a defender can deflect Problem 4 with 'we're working on better coordinates for that' - when in fact no coordinate fix can address it.
holes_found.recommendation: Add one sentence to Problem 4 closer (between the sphere-in-disguise line and the §7.1 cross-ref): 'This is a separate failure from the coordinate-formula debate - a factor of 8-9 rather than V12's 2x cross-equator error - and it follows from the disc radius itself rather than from any coordinate choice. It cannot be patched by a better V13/V14 formula; only by replacing the disc radius, which would unmake the model.' Makes explicit that no coordinate refinement can rescue this.

holes_found.description: 'SPHERE-IN-DISGUISE' CLOSER VULNERABLE TO 'WE PREDICT DIFFERENTLY ON OTHER TESTS' REBUTTAL. The closer rhetoric - 'a flat-disc metric that compresses distances by exactly the factor needed to match a sphere is a sphere in disguise - at that point the dome has lost its geometric distinctiveness and become a renamed globe projection' - is rhetorically catchy but a sophisticated defender will counter: 'Our model is distinguished from the globe on independent tests: firmament-dome physics, sun altitude/Bishop's ring, horizon dip, day/night asymmetry. Metric-equivalence for nautical distance does not erase those distinctions; we are a different physical model that embeds globe-like nautical geometry as a constraint from circumnavigation measurements.' The kill-shot does not pre-empt this rejoinder. The 'renamed globe projection' framing risks being quoted-and-rebutted as strawman.
holes_found.recommendation: Either soften the closer to 'on the geometric-distance test, the dome must adopt globe-equivalent compressions, which collapses the geometric content of its disc-radius parameter on that test' (more precise, weaker rhetoric) - OR strengthen by pre-empting: 'A defender might reply that the dome remains distinctive on other tests - sun altitude, horizon dip, firmament dome - but those tests inherit the same disc-radius parameter, so a metric that erases distance-distinctiveness inherits the erasure across all geometry-derived predictions.' Operator's call on rhetoric vs precision tradeoff.

holes_found.description: 'CALIBRATION-AT-SYD-PER SUCCEEDS WHILE GEOMETRY-AT-RIM FAILS' LINKAGE IS UNDERSTATED. The Summary closer says: 'Test 1's point is that the Sydney-Perth calibration succeeds in fitting one railway distance while the geometry it rides on top of fails the simplest rim test by ~800%.' This frames the relationship between Problem 1 (calibration) and Problem 4 (rim) but a defender will reasonably argue 'SYD-PER is in our fitted domain; the rim is outside it - you are testing extrapolation outside the calibration set, which we never claimed to handle.' The kill-shot does not explicitly defend against this domain-restriction escape. The actual rebuttal: the disc radius (20,015 km) is the SAME parameter that fixes the rim AND that enters the coordinate system used for SYD-PER computation. The two tests are not independent - they share a parameter.
holes_found.recommendation: Add (in the Summary closer or as a sentence in Problem 4): 'The disc radius (20,015 km) that fixes the rim is also the parameter the V13 coordinate system uses to map every other city - Sydney-Perth included. The rim test and the SYD-PER calibration share parameters; failing the rim impeaches every coordinate the same radius helped place.' Forecloses the 'outside-our-fitted-domain' escape.

holes_found.description: '~800%' ROUNDING. Problem 4 closer says 'fails the simplest rim test by ~800%.' Actual computation: (111,800 - 13,700) / 13,700 = 716%. 'Factor-of-eight' (integer multiplier) = 8.16x, which equals 716% as percentage difference. '~800%' rounds 716% up to 800%, which a literal-minded defender could nitpick as overstating by ~12%. Inconsistent with the more precise 'factor of eight at the coast and a factor of nine at the rim' a few sentences earlier.
holes_found.recommendation: Tighten to 'fails the simplest rim test by a factor of 8-9' or 'fails the simplest rim test by over 700%' - either is internally consistent. Minor cosmetic; not worth a dedicated patch but include if doing any above hole fixes.

holes_found.description: CROSS-REFERENCE DUPLICATION RISK. The kill-shot closes Problem 4 with 'See §7.1 for the full derivation' - and §7.1 contains essentially the same prose at greater length. Acceptable layered disclosure (kill-shot=summary, §7.1=derivation) but creates maintenance burden: any future §7.1 strengthening must be parallel-ported to Test 1, and the c2 -> c3 -> c4 cycle has demonstrated this cost (ISS-2457, this very review). Structural fix would be to make Test 1's Problem 4 a deliberate excerpt with explicit 'For the full argument including the projection-defence and V22 concession, see §7.1' (which would also close hole 1 above). Not blocking; flagging for operator's structural-debt log.

stronger_arguments.description: Use a SPECIFIC documented Antarctic circumnavigation. Jon Sanders made multiple solo circumnavigations through the Southern Ocean (1981-1988 triple non-stop ~71,000 nautical miles ~131,500 km for 3 laps, ~43,800 km per lap at ~50 S). Antarctic Cup course (around 60 S) standard ~20,000 km. Either is a real ship logbook and immune to 'you cited a parallel, not a measurement.' At 43,800 km the dome's 111,800 km is still 2.5x too long; at 20,000 km it is 5.6x too long. Less headline shock than 'factor of 8,' but airtight against citation attack.

deeper_analysis: EXP-554 integration is the third cycle of work on this kill-shot (c1 -> c2 -> c3 -> c4 here). Pattern: each cycle closes headline asymmetries between Part 5 Test 1 and §7.1 but reveals smaller gradient asymmetries. c1 (2026-04-06) flagged rim circumnavigation as missing; c2 (2026-06-01) re-flagged plus added 'three new free parameters' / 'black box' asymmetries; EXP-554 closed all three c2 sub-points; c4 (this review) finds three smaller asymmetries (projection-defence pre-empt, V22 concession, separate-failure framing) - all live in §7.1 but were not in c2 h2's enumeration. Consistent with curmudgeon-review behaviour generally: each cycle catches the next layer down. NOT consistent with a stable end-state - Part 5 Test 1 is asymptotically approaching §7.1 in argumentative coverage rather than reaching a fixed point. Structural question (Hole 9): is the right answer to keep parallel-porting (high maintenance cost) or to make Test 1 an explicit summary that defers to §7.1 for load-bearing pre-empts? Operator previously rejected (b) consolidation in c2's recommendation (chose path (a) port). Recommendation here: complete the port - close Hole 1 (projection-defence) and Hole 3 (V22 concession) - then accept Test 1 and §7.1 are intentional duplicates and add maintenance note to operator's structural-debt log. The empirical-anchor weakness (Hole 2) is the most defender-quotable; recommend fix in both Test 1 AND §7.1 simultaneously, since both share the unsourced '~13,700 km' claim. Note for tinker: this run completed within ~10 minutes after fresh clone, suggesting deep-attack class is correctly singleton-scheduled. Confidence on verdict (0.86) unchanged from c2 - headline argument decisive; remaining work is patch-the-seams.

summary_for_decider: Deep-attack review of KILLSHOT-SH after EXP-554. ALL THREE c2 h2 sub-points closed (rim arg present, structural-elements wording, black-box framing). Verdict (Misleading) unchanged at confidence 0.86. NINE new holes found: 2 major, 4 moderate, 3 minor. Major: (1) projection-defence pre-empt missing from Part 5 (present in §7.1) - defender can strawman 'AE isn't our mapping'; (2) '~13,700 km measured' anchor unsourced and conflates 70 S parallel with circumnavigation - defender will quote against us. Recommend porting two §7.1 sentences (the 'any monotonic mapping...' pre-empt and V22 concession) into Part 5 Test 1, and either citing a specific circumnavigation record or disclosing that 13,700 km is the 70 S parallel calculation. Both fixes are <100 words total; both must also be applied to §7.1 in the case of the empirical-anchor (same problem in both sections). No verdict change recommended. No carry-forward c2 issues - c2 h2 is fully closed; new holes are first-time findings. Test 1 is asymptotically approaching §7.1's argumentative coverage but not yet at parity - operator may want to consider whether kill-shots should be deliberate excerpts with parallel-sync convention (structural-debt note in Hole 9). Class: deep-attack handled correctly as singleton.
